claims.claim: Researchers from Stanford University and NVIDIA developed CLM-8B, a non-generative dual-encoder model architecture for autonomous AI agents.
claims.notes: Joint release between Stanford and NVIDIA research teams.

claims.claim: CLM-8B is formulated as a fast intuitive "System 1" decision layer that scores actions in vector space rather than generating autoregressive tokens one-by-one.
claims.notes: Contrastive learning replaces autoregressive next-token prediction.

claims.claim: The architecture uses a frozen Qwen3-8B foundation with two lightweight 20-million-parameter trainable projection heads for state and action embeddings.
claims.notes: Decoupled state and action encoders enable pre-caching reusable actions.

claims.claim: CLM-8B executes agent decisions up to 9x faster than competitive models like Jev, reaching up to 13x speedup on large action candidate sets.
claims.notes: Empirically benchmarked on latency vs traditional LLM agents.

claims.claim: On coding agent evaluations, CLM-8B achieved 81.6% on DeepSWE and 87.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
claims.notes: Matches or exceeds heavier generative models on agentic tool calling.

claims.claim: CLM-8B is not an open-ended conversational chatbot or long-form prose writer; it is strictly an agent action selection model.
claims.notes: CRITICAL EDITORIAL BOUNDARY: Clarify this is for decision scoring, not chatting.

uncertainties: Tool-calling accuracy exhibits a small trade-off under extreme candidate diversity without fine-tuning.
